verses.text: "The sin of Judah is written with an iron pen, carved with a diamond point on the tablets of their hearts and on the horns of their altars.
Even their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside the green trees on the high hills.
My mountain in the countryside, I will give away your riches and all your treasures as plunder, along with your high places, because of the sin throughout your land.
Through your own fault you will lose the inheritance I gave you. I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have started a fire in my anger that will burn forever."
This is what the LORD says: "Cursed is the person who trusts in mere humans, who depends on human strength and whose heart turns away from the LORD.
That person will be like a bush in the desert. They will not see good things when they come. They will live in the dry places of the wilderness, in a salty land where no one lives.
But blessed is the person who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in the LORD.

They will be like a tree planted by the water that sends out its roots by the stream. It is not afraid when the heat comes. Its leaves stay green. It does not worry in a year of drought, and it never stops producing fruit."
The heart is more deceitful than anything else, and it is very sick. Who can understand it?
"I, the LORD, search the heart and test the mind, to reward each person according to their ways, according to what their actions deserve."

Like a partridge that sits on eggs it did not lay, so is the person who gets rich in unfair ways. In the middle of their life their riches will leave them, and in the end they will prove to be a fool.
A glorious throne, lifted high from the beginning, is the place of our holy temple.
LORD, you are the hope of Israel. All who leave you will be put to shame. Those who turn away from you will be written in the dust, because they have left the LORD, the spring of living water.
Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved, for you are the one I praise.
They keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come true now!"
But I have not run away from being your shepherd. I have not wished for the day of disaster. You know what I have said. It is all open before you.
Do not be a terror to me. You are my safe place in the day of disaster.
Let those who chase after me be put to shame, but keep me from shame. Let them be terrified, but keep me from terror. Bring on them the day of disaster. Destroy them with double destruction.
This is what the LORD said to me: "Go and stand at the People's Gate, where the kings of Judah go in and out. Then stand at all the other gates of Jerusalem.
Say to them, 'Listen to the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah, all you people of Judah, and everyone living in Jerusalem who comes through these gates.
This is what the LORD says: Be careful not to carry any load on the Sabbath day or bring it in through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath or do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.
But they did not listen or pay attention. They were stubborn and would not listen or accept correction.
But if you carefully obey me, says the LORD, and do not bring a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath, but keep the Sabbath day holy by not doing any work on it,

then kings who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this city with their officials. They will ride in chariots and on horses, along with the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem. And this city will be lived in forever.

People will come from the towns of Judah and the villages around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the western foothills, from the hill country, and from the south. They will bring burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, incense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

But if you do not obey me and keep the Sabbath day holy, if you carry a load as you come through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will set fire to its gates. The fire will burn up the strong buildings of Jerusalem, and it will not be put out.'"
